title: Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) — Internal Launch Brief (Draft Slides)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) Launch
Internal launch brief (Host API + Console + DX)

Speaker notes:
- Goal today: align on messaging + demo narrative + how we’ll measure attribution + activation post-launch.
- This is PLG-first but designed to open doors for Dedicated/Private follow-ups.


Slide 2 — What shipped (v1)
- Opinionated templates with “production shape” from day one
  - RAG service + ingestion pipeline
  - Agents (tool calling + structured output)
  - Combined RAG+Agent workflow (retrieval as a tool)
- Observability pack: dashboards + alerts + trace exemplars
- Safe defaults baked in: timeouts, retries/backoff, 429 handling, secrets guidance, PII notes
- Local run + containerized run paths (Docker Compose); minimal K8s manifests

Speaker notes:
- Emphasize consistency across templates: same env var contract and telemetry schema.
- Not a framework; these are starting points that look like “real apps.”


Slide 3 — The customer problem (JTBD)
- “I have an API key; now help me ship something real.”
- Common failure modes we’re directly addressing:
  - No retries/timeouts → flaky demos + tickets
  - Streaming disconnect confusion
  - 429 behavior unclear (and customers accidentally DDoS themselves)
  - No request correlation IDs → debugging is painful
  - No cost/latency visibility → teams can’t forecast unit economics

Speaker notes:
- Anchor this in support and onboarding friction: these templates are a supportability investment.


Slide 4 — Primary audience + positioning
Primary users:
- Software/ML engineers building LLM features into a product
Positioning:
- “Fastest path from API key to observable production-ready app”
What we are NOT:
- A managed agent runtime
- A one-size-fits-all framework

Speaker notes:
- Keep language consistent with docs site: “templates” and “quickstarts,” not “framework.”


Slide 5 — Messaging pillars (internal)
1) Production-minded defaults
- Timeouts, retries/backoff, idempotency patterns, graceful shutdown, health checks
2) Observable by default (Console-aligned)
- Traces + structured logs + cost/latency metrics + error taxonomy
3) Safe by default
- Tool allow-list, schema validation, PII handling guidance, secrets patterns
4) Path to scale
- Dedicated/Private considerations called out (routing/fallback policies, capacity isolation, audit expectations)

Speaker notes:
- “Observable by default” is the differentiation vs. random community templates.


Slide 6 — Template catalog (talk track)
RAG template:
- Ingestion worker + query service
- Default vector backend (v1) + adapter interface for extension
Agents template:
- Tool calling guardrails + tool timeout wrappers
- Structured output validation for tool responses
Combined template:
- Retrieval as a tool; planner/executor flow
- Prompt injection awareness (don’t blindly follow retrieved instructions)

Speaker notes:
- Avoid naming specific vendors too heavily in launch messaging; highlight adapter pattern.


Slide 7 — Demo goals (what success looks like)
In 10 minutes, show:
- A working RAG + agent flow
- Streaming response
- Request ID propagation + trace in Console
- Token-level cost/latency breakdown
- Error handling: simulated 429 + backoff behavior is understandable

Speaker notes:
- We are optimizing for “wow + trust.” People need to believe it won’t fall apart in production.


Slide 8 — Demo flow (recommended script)
0) Pre-flight
- Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and baseline env vars
- Start docker compose (app + vector db)
1) Ingest docs
- Run ingestion worker
- Show logs include request_id + route + component
2) Query + tool call
- User asks a question that triggers retrieval tool
- Show tool allow-list decision + tool timeout wrapper behavior
3) Open Console
- Show trace (end-to-end) with key attributes
- Show dashboard panels: p95 latency, token usage, error class breakdown

Speaker notes:
- Keep the demo stable: use a small fixed doc set, and a deterministic-ish prompt.


Slide 9 — Console tie-in (what to highlight)
Highlight panels/flows that match template telemetry:
- Latency p50/p95 by route + model
- Token usage and estimated cost by route/tenant
- Error rates by class (timeout vs upstream vs validation)
- 429 visibility (count + rate) and “what to do next” guidance
- Trace exemplars for a successful RAG request and a tool call request

Speaker notes:
- We want the audience to see: “Templates are first-class citizens in Console.”


Slide 10 — Safe defaults (callouts)
Defaults we intentionally chose:
- Timeouts set everywhere (client + tool calls + vector store)
- Bounded retries with exponential backoff + jitter
- Rate limit handling is explicit (429 backoff + surface guidance)
- Secrets are never committed; .env example only; CI secret scanning expected
- Logging hygiene: correlation IDs + no raw prompt dumps by default; PII guidance in README

Speaker notes:
- Message: “you can copy/paste without copying unsafe patterns.”


Slide 11 — Release plan + ownership
Launch surfaces:
- Docs-site landing page + walkthroughs
- GitHub repos (redwood-quickstarts + redwood-examples)
- Observability pack import instructions
Ownership post-launch:
- DX owns templates + docs coordination
- SDK team owns helper behavior and version compatibility
- Console team owns dashboards pack alignment + telemetry contract changes

Speaker notes:
- Be explicit internally: fixes will be rapid during launch week; then shift to scheduled releases.


Slide 12 — Versioning + compatibility (what we’ll say)
- Templates are versioned independently (tags + changelog)
- Compatibility matrix:
  - Template version ↔ SDK version ↔ recommended API features
- Deprecations:
  - “warn then remove” policy; docs callouts for migration

Speaker notes:
- Keep it simple publicly; internally we need this to avoid drift and broken snippets.


Slide 13 — Attribution: what we need to know
We need to answer:
- Which acquisition channel drove template adoption?
- Which template drove activation (first success + repeat usage)?
- Where do users drop off (install, config, ingest, query, deploy)?

Speaker notes:
- Attribution is not just marketing UTMs; it’s product telemetry + docs analytics + repo events.


Slide 14 — Attribution sources (proposed)
1) Docs
- UTM parameters on template CTAs (source/medium/campaign)
- Track events: view template page → click “Use this template” → copy env example
2) GitHub
- Link clicks to repo + release notes (via docs UTMs)
- (Optional) star/fork as weak signal; not primary
3) Product (Hosted API + Console)
- Template user-agent / x-redwood-template header
- Distinct “template_id” tag (rag_py, rag_ts, agents_py, combined_py, etc.)
- Correlate: first API call after landing page click (time window)

Speaker notes:
- The most reliable signal is request tags emitted from the template itself.


Slide 15 — Activation metrics (north stars)
Primary (PLG):
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS): target < 15 minutes
- First successful run rate: % of new API keys that produce at least 1 successful response from template within 24h
Secondary:
- Deploy conversion: % who run container/K8s path within 7 days
- Repeat usage: day-7 active keys that used templates at least 2 distinct days
Quality/safety:
- Error rate during onboarding (by class)
- 429 rate during onboarding cohort (should go down as defaults guide behavior)

Speaker notes:
- Tie to project goals: <60 minutes to deploy to managed env is a narrative goal; measure proxy signals.


Slide 16 — Metric definitions (internal consistency)
New API key cohort:
- “new_key_created_at” from signup
Template success event:
- First request with template_id where HTTP 2xx and non-empty completion
TTFS:
- first_success_ts - key_created_ts
First run rate:
- count(keys with first_success within 24h) / count(new keys)

Speaker notes:
- We need to avoid counting “hello world” outside templates as template activation.


Slide 17 — Event taxonomy (what templates will emit)
Required tags/fields (high level):
- request_id
- tenant_id (or anonymous install id for local dev)
- template_id + template_version
- route (ingest/query/tool)
- model + region (if applicable)
- token_usage (prompt/complete) and estimated cost
- error_class + error_code (timeout, rate_limited, validation, upstream, network)

Speaker notes:
- Cardinality control matters: keep template_id small and controlled; avoid raw user inputs.


Slide 18 — Launch dashboard (internal)
Panels we’ll use during launch week:
- Template traffic volume by template_id
- TTFS distribution (p50/p90)
- Error rate by class (with top 3 stack traces / messages bucketed)
- 429 rate + backoff effectiveness (retry success rate)
- Streaming disconnect rate (proxy for “it feels broken”)
- Cost per successful first run (sanity check)

Speaker notes:
- This is how we’ll decide if we need hotfix docs, SDK tweaks, or template patches.


Slide 19 — FAQ / expected questions (and answers)
Q: Does this work for Dedicated/Private?
- A: Yes; templates include notes and K8s manifests; Dedicated/Private have additional networking/identity/audit constraints.
Q: Which vector DB is supported?
- A: v1 supports a default + adapter interface; we’ll expand based on demand.
Q: Are we endorsing agent autonomy?
- A: No; we demonstrate tool calling with allow-lists, timeouts, and schema validation.
Q: Will templates leak PII?
- A: Defaults avoid logging raw prompts; PII guidance included; encourage redaction and retention controls.

Speaker notes:
- Keep answers short; route detailed questions to docs + security guidance.


Slide 20 — Launch checklist (internal)
- Docs pages merged + code snippets auto-validated
- Observability pack import instructions tested end-to-end
- SDK helper versions pinned in templates
- CI smoke tests green against staging
- Support playbook updated (common 429 + streaming issues)
- Launch-week owner rotation and Slack channel set

Speaker notes:
- We should not ship without the snippet validation; drift is a top support driver.


Slide 21 — Ask from teams
DX:
- Be on deck for launch-week support and template patch releases
SDK:
- Hold stable retry/timeout behaviors; avoid breaking changes during launch window
Console/Telemetry:
- Ensure dashboards align with telemetry contract; confirm trace join behavior
Support/CS:
- Funnel onboarding issues into a single intake tag: “quickstart-templates”

Speaker notes:
- This is a cross-functional launch; the product surface is bigger than docs.


Slide 22 — Appendix: proposed internal comms blurb
“We’re launching production-minded Quickstart Templates for RAG + Agents. These templates take you from API key to an observable app in minutes, with safe defaults (timeouts/retries/tool allow-lists) and a Console-ready telemetry contract. Use them for onboarding, demos, and reference implementations—and please file issues with ‘template_id’ and request_id so we can debug fast.”

Speaker notes:
- This is the message for #announcements and for internal enablement.


Open questions / TODOs (for reviewers)
- Confirm final template IDs and naming (match docs + telemetry)
- Decide whether to include template version in user-agent vs custom header
- Confirm launch-week dashboard ownership (who watches what + when)
- Finalize which demo environment we standardize on (local vs staging)
